title: The category of standard h coverings of an affine limit is the colimit of the categories of standard h coverings of the approximating schemes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme T written as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes T_i, the lemma asserts three approximation statements: a standard h covering of T descends to a standard h covering of some T_i, morphisms of standard h coverings descend after increasing the index, and two morphisms with equal base change to T become equal at some index; equivalently the category of standard h coverings of T is the colimit over I of those of T_i (statement lines 10767-10795). The proof reduces the first statement to a single assertion: if a finite family of finitely presented morphisms with affine sources becomes an h covering after base change to T, then it is already an h covering after base change to some T_i (proof lines 10797-10809). For this it uses Lemma labelled lemma-approximate-h-cover to choose a finitely presented proper surjective Y -> T together with a finite affine open covering refining the given family, and then Limits, Lemmas labelled limits-lemma-eventually-proper, limits-lemma-descend-surjective and limits-lemma-descend-opens to descend Y -> T, the cover and the refinement to some T_{i'}, so that the descended family is an h covering (proof lines 10811-10827). Descending the approximating proper cover and reading the h covering property off the descended refinement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
